chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from al-Hasan ibn Yusuf, from Salih ibn 'Uqba, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him),

He said: The people are of three types: Arab, Mawla (client/follower), and 'Alaj (foreigner/stranger). As for the Arab, it is us; as for the Mawla, it is those who are loyal to us; and as for the 'Alaj, it is those who disavow us and are hostile to us.

key_terms.عَرَبِيّ: Arab (specifically referring to the Ahl al-Bayt in this context)
key_terms.عَلَج: Alaj (foreigner or stranger, referring to those hostile to the Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.مَوْلَى: Mawla (client or follower, referring to loyal supporters)
key_terms.نَاصَبَنَا: Were hostile / declared war against us

ai.seo_question: What are the three categories of people according to Imam Musa al-Kadhim (a.s.)?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS) redefines the classical Arabic terms 'Arab', 'Mawla', and 'Alaj' through a Shia theological lens, shifting the focus from lineage to affinity with the Ahl al-Bayt. This categorization serves as a foundational principle for Shia identity, distinguishing the Imams themselves as the true 'Arabs', their devoted followers as 'Mawla', and their detractors as 'Alaj'. It underscores the concept of *Wala'* and *Bara'* as the primary markers of religious belonging rather than ethnic or tribal origin.

en.basel-kadem: 69.	My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Muhammed bin Isa, that he said: We were told by Yunus bin Abdul-Rahman, that he said: We were told by Hammad bin Isa, that he said: We were told by Ja’far bin Muhammed, from his father, peace be upon them both, that he said: Jabir bin Abdullah said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, say to Ali bin Abi Talib (a.s) before his death with three (days), 'The peace of Allah be upon you, O father of the Two Aromas. I bequeath you with regards to my Aroma of this world, for soon will your pillars collapse, and Allah is the my Trustee upon you.' Then, when the Messenger of Allah, (s.w.) was taken, Ali said: This is one of my pillars about whom the Messenger of Allah spoke to me. Then, when Fatima (a.s) died, Ali (a.s) said: 'This is the second pillar about whom the Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, spoke.'"
